pk.context: 300 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: peach, flat-faced hexagonal tablet with a score bar

tell: Its active metabolite oxypurinol, with a half-life of about 15 hours, also inhibits xanthine oxidase and outlasts the parent.

clues.text: About 90% is absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract. The kidneys are the main route of elimination, and about 20% of the ingested dose is excreted in feces.
Molecular weight 136.11 with a water solubility of 80.0 mg/dL at 37°C, greater in alkaline solution.
Marketed under an NDA in 100, 200 and 300 mg strengths, each with functional scoring.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated after any hypersensitivity to it or its ingredients; skin rash is the most frequent reaction, with diarrhea and nausea also common.
Primary or secondary gout, patients on cancer therapy for leukemia, lymphoma or solid tumors, and recurrent calcium oxalate stones with high daily excretion.
Inhibits xanthine oxidase, the enzyme converting hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid, so less uric acid is produced.
The generic name begins with A and has eleven letters.
